notes.decision: Translated as 'ripenings' per accumulated vocabulary. The agricultural-seasonal context (paired with figs and tree-fruits, in a passage about zodiacal influence) confirms the seasonal-ripening sense over Crum's 'sickness/scab.'
Translated as 'come into being' (= ϣⲱⲡⲉ). The subject 'they' refers back to the previous page's discussion of zodiac-related cosmic phenomena.

Greek loanwords for Scorpio (Σκορπίος), Pisces (Ἰχθύς), and Cancer (Καρκίνος) — the three water signs. The text correlates these with diminishing of waters, then the air signs (Gemini/Libra/Aquarius) with diminishing of humanity, displaying classical astrological element-correspondence.
Translated as 'diminishing' — likely cognate with ⲇⲱⲭⲃⲉ 'diminish' (in glossary, Crum 511a). The substantival ⲟⲩⲃⲱⲭⲃⲉ functions as 'a diminishing/decrease.'

Translated as 'waters' (homograph of 'counsels' but here in clearly hydrological context — diminishing of waters under water-zodiac influence). Per glossary entry distinguishing the two homographs in this kephalaion.

Translated tentatively as 'year-of-failure / year of scarcity.' Etymology unclear: ⲣⲙ̄ⲡⲉ ('year') + ϣⲉⲗⲣⲉ. Possibly related to ϣⲗⲟ 'fail, be exhausted' or to ϣⲗⲱⲣ 'fresh' (Crum). The agricultural-zodiacal context of waters diminishing supports a famine/scarcity sense. Flagged as proposed term.

Greek loanwords for Gemini (Δίδυμος 'twins'), Libra (Ζυγός 'yoke'), and Aquarius (Ὑδροχόος 'water-pourer') — the three air signs. Form a paired triad with the water signs in line 3, demonstrating the elemental zodiacal scheme.

Translated as 'the imprint of humanity' — ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ in correspondential register denotes the seal/imprint by which humanity is configured cosmically. Per glossary: 'imprint/seal.' The lack and diminishing affecting humanity under air-sign influence parallels the water-diminishing under water-signs.

Greek ἀναβιβάζων 'ascending node' — astronomical term for the lunar nodes (Caput Draconis et Cauda). 'The two anabibazons' refers to the ascending and descending lunar nodes, traditionally the cosmological 'dragon's head and tail.' Retained as Greek technical term.

'The Dry one and the Moist one' — capitalized as cosmic principles. ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲩⲃⲉ corresponds to ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲇⲃⲉ in glossary ('the moist one'). The dry/moist dyad here is identified directly with Father/Mother — the primordial cosmic pair. Direct correspondential identification.

'The work takes light upon him' — referring to sun/moon. The cosmic 'work' (= the soteriological refining-economy) draws light upon the sun and moon, hence they are reckoned among the plunderers (= those who plunder light from darkness).

Translated as 'not being reckoned' — taking ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ as a partitive/relational ('to him/it') modulated by negative ⲉⲛ. The sense: sun and moon are not counted in the dark cosmos with stars and zodiac, since they belong to the dominion (ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲃ) of light. Reading uncertain in fine detail; structure clear.

notes.decision: Chapter title spread across lines 23-26 in decorated layout with Ⲟ markers. 'Concerning the body, that it was established with respect to the likeness of the cosmos.' The microcosm-macrocosm correspondence is the topic: the human body IS in the likeness of the cosmos. ⲥⲙⲛⲧϩ = ⲥⲙⲟⲛⲧ̄ (qualitative of ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ 'establish'). ⲟⲩⲃⲉ here = 'with respect to, against (in correspondence with).'
Standard Manichaean narrative formula 'on one of the occasions/times.' ⲟⲩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲏⲩ = 'one of the times.'
'Assembly' — per accumulated vocabulary. The Apostle teaches in the church (ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ) in the midst of the assembled congregation.
